intended_object: The probability density of the standard arcsine distribution on (0,1): f(x) = 1/(π√(x(1−x))) for 0 < x < 1, and 0 elsewhere. This comes from the docstring and the name; the module also builds `arcsinePDF` and `arcsineMeasure` from it.
explanation:
The body is exactly the textbook density of the standard arcsine law: 1/(π√(x(1−x))) on the open interval (0,1) and 0 outside it. The endpoints 0 and 1 are a null set and the density blows up there, so setting the value to 0 there is harmless.

Mathlib has no definition of the arcsine distribution. It does have `ProbabilityTheory.betaPDFReal`, and the arcsine law is Beta(1/2, 1/2): since B(1/2, 1/2) = Γ(1/2)²/Γ(1) = π, the two densities agree. That is a special case of a more general family, not the same declaration, so I leave the counterpart field empty.

The definition is not too narrow. It is a specific, named distribution, and the standard arcsine law is the usual object in the literature. The version on a general interval [a,b] is just an affine change of variables of this one.
